exposure: paralysis that gradually improved without worsening
cohort: The study included patients under 1 year of age presenting with suspected or previously diagnosed obstetrical brachial plexus palsy (OBPP) at 2 tertiary children's centers in Osaka between 1994 and 2021.
finding: The study identified key characteristics (paralysis from birth, paralysis following an anatomic distribution, and paralysis that gradually improved without worsening) for accurate OBPP diagnosis and a key indicator (joint contracture immediately after birth) for ruling it out, suggesting an MRI of the brachial plexus when these criteria are not met.
birth_weight: Yes, differences were found in birth weight between groups.
gest_age: Yes, differences were found in gestational age between groups.
